steps.text: Are you awake, pup?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I don't know what's sadder for Umberto: To slowly waste away from age and illness, or to watch how his pups get dumber with each generation.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: How sad and pathetic, humans.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Y-You're—
The memory is blurry, but Luchino remembers the voice.
The night that Umberto brought him back to Tailor de Montano...
Sitting on a chair, Luchino looked blankly at the unfamiliar room before him, filled with various fabrics and tools.
Umberto was outside talking to someone. Suddenly, he turns around, and through the window Luchino thought Umberto was showing him to someone else, but does not see who it is.
His grandfather, his only living relation. Luchino feels his stomach churn with nervousness.
Then, he hears a voice mixed with anger and resignation exclaim, 'Shameless human! Up to the same old tricks again!'

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Are you nonno's... friend?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: Friend?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: Friend, teacher, master, employer, client... my relationship with Umberto is not so easily defined.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I am the master of these wilds, pup, and your grandfather is my Fang.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: A most incompetent one, I might add...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Guess I'm really getting old.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: No matter how long I sat by the worktable, the nights never felt this long...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: And I would have noticed you coming in. When?

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Ten minutes ago.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Do you mind if I kept working while we talked?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I was delayed by an old friend's unexpected visit. I must hurry and finish the most important work on this suit.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Luchino can take care of the final touch-ups himself.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I smell no scent of wolf from you, even a little bit.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Nor have you masked it in any unusual way. I was watching, I can tell.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: ...Are you really the last true wolf?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: True wolf? Ah, you mean the Fangs.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Yes, you've come to the right place, young one.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I observed Umberto for a long time.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I watched him serve customers of every kind, casually putting his scissors through some of their throats while taking measurement, without getting a single drop of blood on himself.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: He was not a warrior, like Ingrid, but he was smart and knew how to make the most of who he was.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: He was also good at disguising himself. He spent most of his time in Tailor de Montano, and he was equally in demand as a tailor as he was as an assassin.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: That's why I chose him. I told him about the Signori dei Lupi, and the existence of the game.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Nonno's stories were true!

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: You're the wolf from the stories... no wonder he wanted to leave the famiglia. He was the Signore dei Lupi's chosen, the most special tailor in Siracusa. He sure is very lucid!

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Did nonno accept your deal?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: No Fang can reject the Signori dei Lupi.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: But Umberto set a condition.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: C-Condition?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: He was not the first Fang to try to bargain with the Signori dei Lupi. Impertinent fools! I know a hundred ways to destroy them and find someone else to take their place.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: What did nonno want to do?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: Umberto wanted to raise his pup to adulthood, before delivering my victory.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: His wife had passed away, he said, and his young pup, Luca, was too young to survive without him.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: That was it?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: That was it. I agreed.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: The society of humans was no more dangerous than the wilderness. I did not imagine it would take up so much of his time and energy.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I visited the tailor's shop from time to time to make sure he was not deceiving me.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: That day, Umberto shut down his assassination business, devoting all his time to the sewing machine, fabric, and the young pup as it grew.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: But his hands were still steady, and his eyes still sharp. Therefore, I kept my promise.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I needed a Fang that would not break, not easily-distracted prey. I gave him time. I had plenty of it.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: But papa...

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: Died meaninglessly.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I gave Umberto plenty of time to recover from the shock.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: It may not have been how Umberto planned it, but at least now he was no longer burdened. And so one night I visited him again, and demanded that he hold up his end of the bargain.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: But my Fang once again bargained with me—
The Signore dei Lupi pauses and glares at the young tailor before him.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Do you mean...

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: He learned that his pup had a pup of its own, the last family he had... He wanted to raise you to adulthood too, before the hunt begins.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: 'Shameless human! Up to the same old tricks again!'

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: That was you...

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: This time, I did not assent. But he seems to have forgotten who he was, and who I was to him!

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: Every time I pressed him, he babbles something like how life keeps repeating itself, while shamelessly promising that he will hold up his end of the bargain.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: But nonno was never in good health, as long as I could remember.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: My Fang could hardly defend himself now, much less deliver my victory.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: The only result of my patience was that he had grown old.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Nonno actually—

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I know he's only ever cared about his shop, the suits he made, and the people he loved.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: That's why he did those things, which he was never made for... Umberto was a fool. I was wrong about him.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Why are you telling me all this, Signore dei Lupi?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: All my effort and patience have only earned me an eternity of scorn from the pack for breaking the rules of the game.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: You are his pup. Now you must face punishment.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: P-Punishment...

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: All your efforts tonight will be futile, whether you are trying to destroy the weapons, or destroy the ship.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: Look down at your chest...
Luchino looks down and sees that the front of his jacket has flown open. He must have dropped his button in the chaos.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: Whatever you want to become, pup, learn to sew your own buttons first.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: Now, get lost. Go back to Umberto!

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: You are a terrible actor, Vargo.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: That mock anger... were you afraid we would harm that pup?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: He was not part of the game—

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: Have you forgotten the decision of the pack, Vargo?

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: The Signori dei Lupi shall stay here until this round is decided, and shall not intervene in any manner, or else...

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I've already lost, Caesar.
The silvery Signore dei Lupi suddenly looks up.
He casts his gaze towards a corner of the city, a city engulfed in revelry, the night sky bright as day. No one notices that a certain cloud has dispersed.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: The wind brings a familiar scent. Red has done her work.

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: I won't be shameless like Zaaro, Caesar. I have gone against the decision of the pack, and I shall accept my punishment.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: Are you mourning your Fang?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: Just bitter about losing.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I wouldn't have found you without grandma's help.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Grandma?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: That's how you call your wolf? I've never thought of them as being particularly kindly...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: But then, Vargo must have figured out a long time ago that he was being deceived. There's a soft heart there, underneath the surface.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: You won't resist either?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Either?

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: The last true wolf that I killed didn't resist.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: She just watched me pierce her chest as she cuddled her limp leg.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: She sighed and muttered, 'Finally, no need to live in fear anymore...'

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Sounds like death was a relief to her.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Well, it's not as if I stood any chance if I tried to resist. Besides, I don't mind this chat going on for a while longer. It would ruin this new suit if we started fighting right now.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Phew—almost there.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Measure, cut, shape, trim... that's how plain cloth becomes stylish clothes.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: There are about four hundreds and fifty steps to a standard Siracusa suit, but it doesn't take as much time as one might think, if you go about them step by step, calmly and patiently.
The sound of the sewing machine stops.
The old tailor trims away the protruding threads, gets up from his chair, and walks by the huntress to hang the new suit on the wall.
He sighs, rubs his swollen eyes, and lies down on a sofa in a corner.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Do you mind if I lie down? At this age, I get dizzy whenever I work for an extended period of time.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Grandma was right. True wolves are good at disguising themselves.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I do not understand why you don't smell of wolf, but it doesn't change what you did to grandma.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: You ate grandma's eyes, arms and heart...

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Answer me, true wolf. Why do you engage in such a cruel game?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I see. That's how you understand the game to be like.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I take it you asked the last Fang you killed the same question.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I don't have an answer either, young one. We were all chosen by fate, by happenstance.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Whether it is lies or the truth that accompanies us, however, all of it will converge upon a single end... What will you do when that time comes?

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Find the other true wolf who escaped me.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Her bow is weak. She is no match for me.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: No, what I mean is, what happens when you've killed all the true wolves?

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: The game ends, and grandma is saved.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: *Cough* And what about you? Where will you go from there? What will you do?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Have you been seeking out and killing true wolves all this time?

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: (Waggles ears)

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: No. I was helping Kal'tsit. There are many things at Rhodes Island that I need to do...
The huntress bows her head.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I have wasted too much time.
The cold glint of a dagger shines out of Red's sleeves. She had been holding it all this time.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: You're not afraid, true wolf?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Of course I'm afraid. I always am, whether you're here or not.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: My health has been in a steady decline for a long time. You can't help but be afraid when you know that you don't have much time left.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: But at least I was not like the one you spoke of, who spent a long time waiting for death's visit... that's much scarier than death.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Come to think of it, I didn't really achieve anything in my life.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: A killer who racked up a mountain of blood debts, a father who watched his son die, a grandfather who doesn't know how to teach his grandson, a Fang who never played the game—

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: But I was a good tailor, a lucky old man.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: How many can say that they were doing the work they loved on their deathbed?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I'll leave the finishing touch to you, Luchino...
Red does not raise her dagger. She does not need to.
The old man on the sofa is no longer breathing, as though he had expended his last bit of strength to finish the suit.
Red gazes unblinkingly at the old man's face.
She had seen the deaths of many, all of whom had died with an expression like a mask on their faces.
Even the limp true wolf that was waiting for death had terror on her face when Red came in, which only changed to relief in her final moments.
As for the Reunion members in the Lungmen ruins, and those who invaded Rhodes Island, their faces were twisted from rage or fear.

But the expression on the face of the old man before her never changed, from the moment she walked into the Tailor de Montano, to this very instant. Red was finally certain that he was not disguising himself.
Was the man really who grandma said he was?
The true wolf died before the huntress, but not by the huntress' hand.
Doubt fills Red's heart.
'Where will you go from there? What will you do?'

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I don't understand, Grandma...

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Seems like you hate Siracusa even more than I do.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Ha, you think I'm doing this for revenge?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: No?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I've already said goodbye to my past, Texas.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Maybe there wasn't a formal ceremony, but that doesn't make it any less serious.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I didn't tell you how I became a taxi driver, did I?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I never asked.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hahahaha.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Zaaro and I came across this pile of scrap metal in the wilderness—

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: The two of you got together?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Not many people would interrupt me like this, you know—yes, he's my lackey now.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: A few Siracusans came to Nuova Volsinii together, but started brawling out in the wilderness for no reason, and the car ended up in front of me.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Siracusa invited, so I had to answer, just like you had to return to Volsinii last year.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Are you absolutely sure you're not just recalling the plot of a radio program?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hey, I would be happy to sell the story to a radio station or filmmaker. I think it'll make a good road movie.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: One year ago, I was sitting at that table in the Grey Hall with you when you won this new nomadic city from that Befana Sicilia.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You could call me one of the startup investors in this youthful dream of a new Siracusa.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Of course I needed to be here at the one-year anniversary of Nuova Volsinii, to celebrate with my friends!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You know, I think I deserve some gratitude for all the problems I dealt with behind the scenes to make sure the festival proceeds without a hitch.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Like scattering weapons across the square?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Haha, much more than just that.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Such as?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Such as my dear father, who is quite, let's say, ambitious about his plans for the new city.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I thought Alberto was in custody.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh, come on, haven't you spent enough time in my family to know what a stronzo the Saluzzo don is?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: He wouldn't tolerate the thought of anything being outside his control, despite his failure at Volsinii, despite the vigilance of Nuova Volsinii's City Hall and courts against his interference.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: What did you do?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Took a few things out of his control, that's all...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You'll find out soon enough.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Are you SURE you're not doing this for revenge?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Well, I guess that's a matter of interpretation.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh, and these masked dudes on the square. You remember seeing their boss, that cheerful Perro, in court?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Venezia Junior...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It's often those who despise the game the most who understand the rules most thoroughly.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: He and his Venezia Trucking have never been in violation of the New Urban Management Act. As a matter of fact, he is a two-time winner of the Outstanding Young Entrepreneur award...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: He might hate Siracusa more than either of us, Texas, but he know how to read the winds better than most wolves.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: But what?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I don't like his hairstyle. Too oily.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I prefer Vulpos who aren't so much like wolves.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: A Vulpo mother from a distant land, who returned to Siracusa to seek justice for her Oripathy-afflicted daughter... Touching story, isn't it?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Besides, I happened to know that mother.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: What did you do this time?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Helped her find the culprit. Super easy, barely any inconvenience.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I'm sure you would have done the same.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Sounds like the City Hall should give you a medal for outstanding citizenship.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: What better time to do that than tonight? You can do the honors.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Nah, it wouldn't sit well with my conscience.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: After all, things have gotten to the point where they are, even with all the 'business' that I threw a wrench into.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Now, let's get back to that wager.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Two packs of wolves, increasingly antsy... the end is approaching, Texas.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: ...I'm glad you're here, Ingrid.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The White Wolf of Saluzzo has disrupted our plans. I'm going to the port to deal with matters, lest she ruin everything that Venezia has built in Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I returned my emblem a long time ago. Whatever happens to the famiglia is none of my business.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Drop the act, Antonio. You know why I'm here.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: How did you know it was me?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: When you told me you knew the truth.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: But it was your reaction just now that removed the last vestige of doubt.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Why did you think the Sicilian betrayed you the moment you saw me?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Ah. You tricked me.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Did I?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I had my suspicions, Antonio. If the Tancredis wanted to assassinate the Venezia don, doing it through a child was a highly unreliable method, to say the least...

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: No matter how intricate their plan was, they could not possibly have prepared a doll that Lisa had only fallen in love with half a month ago because of a movie.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: There never was an assassination attempt. You hurt Lisa to agitate me, in order to run me out of the famiglia.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: If that was so—

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Oh, you spared no expenses to make sure that Lisa wanted for nothing when I brought her back. She called you the 'really nice Perro uncle'.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: And the way you beseeched me to come home, after I arrived in Nuova Volsinii...

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You wore your mask perfectly, Antonio. You put on such a natural act that it would put the real thing to shame.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: No, no, it was all real.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Lisa. Lovely, clever child. I was happy from the bottom of my heart when she called me uncle.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: But you were in my way, Ingrid.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I could never have risen in the familglia with you around, much less rise to my present position.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The struggle between Venezia and Tancredi had reached the point where nothing was off-limits. It was a chance I could not afford to miss. Lisa was your only weakness.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: As for why I tried to bring you back after chasing you out from the famiglia, the answer is even simpler...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Times have changed, Ingrid. Be it within the famiglia, or in Nuova Volsinii, Venezia Junior needs a strong right hand.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I even made preparations to sponsor Rhodes Island under the name of Venezia Trucking, in order to allow them to devote their full effort to Lisa's treatment.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: The Don took us in, and we lived together as Venezia for more than a decade. But somehow, you have it in you to hurt the people closest to you—

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Are you going to chastise me for lacking in 'decency', Ingrid?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I'm curious: Do you truly agree with what the old man says, or are you just playing dumb?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: We keep emphasizing 'decency,' acting like we're principled, pretending we're filled with love, and claiming we're so different from the other famiglia!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: But we're no different, are we? Just a bunch of stronzo with blood all over our hands.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: That tailor, Umberto. He's done dirty work after dirty work for the old man, just because he owed the old man one back in the day.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: If decency was really about the famiglia, why did he leave the famiglia to focus on his suits?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: That scar on your face. Is it a mark of honor, or shame? Behind the scar, how many lives were taken in the name of the famiglia?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Who's really decent in this swamp they call Siracusa?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: No one amongst us, at least.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Good. This is the right distance for stabbing.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You really are forthright, Antonio.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I just believe we shouldn't expect something unrealistic from one another.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: What the Siracusans should do is be prepared to lose everything, including those they love the most. That's what I used to admire you for.
A bright flash of light.
The alley they are in is separated from Court Square by a high wall. Only a few dim street lamps illuminate the dark street. The sudden flash of light dazzles Ingrid momentarily.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: This is your Arts? You hid it well.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Doesn't do much, except cause a strong flash of light... it even looks a little silly, doesn't it?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: This is the second time I've ever used it. Without this light, I would not have dodged that bullet while kneeling in the mud of the jungle.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I would not have been able to hold that drunken noble who circled our names away from the list, before cutting his head off.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Anger and distract me with that speech you just gave, then create an opening with the flash—you planned this the moment you saw me, didn't you?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: *Cough*— Ugh—

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: But all my knife found was the omamori you wore on your belt...

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You never had a chance, Antonio, the moment I found out what kind of person you are.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You know, it's funny, I was actually trying to think of an excuse to spare your life on my way here.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Lisa's condition can never be cured, but she has found friends at Rhodes Island, even became an operator for them, working to help other Oripathy patients.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I was worried about Lisa's education, but life has thrown her a bone by the strange deliverance of fate—

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Sorella! Ingrid Venezia! You will insult me with this 'decency', even now?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: You would never have missed my heart if you didn't mean to—*cough*—I shouldn't still be talking.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You're mistaken.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: It's just plain Ingrid. A mother whom you've angered.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: If I was thinking about decency... it was only so that you wouldn't die with any.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I left you alive so that you could bleed to death.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You deserve the pain, Antonio.
Another firework explodes in the skies not far from here, casting its light on Ingrid's face. The parade is about to arrive at the square. Carnevale comes to a climax.
It will be a long time before they find out about the Perro lying on the other side of the wall. Ingrid snickers at the thought.
She walks over the figure lying on the ground and leaves the alley.

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: I still can't get in touch with Antonio! What the hell is going on?

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: And where's Capone at a time like this? I knew you couldn't trust a Sicilian.

steps.name: Mafioso B
steps.text: What do we do now?

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: What do you THINK we do? This ain't a movie when you just call 'Cut!' and go to lunch.

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: Everything has been exposed. City Hall sees us for who we are now. Do you think we can go back to being 'honest citizens of Nuova Volsinii' after this?

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: Complete Antonio's mission, capture the courthouse, then get in touch with the port.

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: Do the reinforcements have their weapons?

steps.name: Mafioso B
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: Good. On my order.

steps.name: Mafioso A
steps.text: Maybe some of us haven't touched a weapon in a year, but we ain't any more out of practice than these cargo-hauling scemo.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Eirene...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: You have the answer?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: It's not the one we want to hear, is it?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Tell Eirene that I'm very sorry about Sommer...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But I will not sign this verdict, and this decision is final.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Nuova Volsinii will not tolerate the crimes of the mafia, but that doesn't mean other people can use the opportunity to achieve their own goals.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I've gotten letters from many friends over the past year. Some of them are judges or lawyers in other cities; others have chosen to pursue a different career.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: They shared a lot of advice with me, about the jurisprudential basis of the New Urban Management Act, and specific room for improvement.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I read many feelings between the lines. Concern, confusion, hope, even envy...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The New Urban Management Act is a unique thing in Siracusa. It is the basis of this city's existence. Many have their eyes upon it; even more have sacrificed for it.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: It's true that it can be powerless at times. But it's especially in times like this that I cannot allow it to become empty words, much less a tool to be exploited.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Still the same old Lavinia.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Hey, Eirene.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Listen to me carefully.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: These people have gotten their hands on weapons. They have become true wolves. The situation is out of control.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: I saw what the mafiosi are capable of when I first came to Siracusa as a kid. They slaughtered my uncle's entire family in just half an hour.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: In a few moments I will release smoke to obstruct their view. Get the guys out of here when that happens. Hand signs, signals, whatever, I know you have a way.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: You'll need to be quick. I've never released smoke in such a large area before, so I don't know how well it will work, or how long I can keep it up.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: The trucks are right behind us. Get in, get away.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: I wasn't with Sommer that night. It's partly my fault that he's dead...

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: There's not much that a luckless loner like me can do, but I can't let my brothers and sisters die here.

steps.name: Truck Driver A
steps.text: That's a gun, not a spanner! Stop pointing it at me—

steps.name: Truck Driver A
steps.text: No, I don't mean point it at yourself!

steps.name: Truck Driver B
steps.text: B-But I don't know how to use it...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Then point it in front of you, Pedro.

steps.name: Truck Driver A
steps.text: But that's—

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Don't worry about it going off, or accidentally touching the switch on some Arts unit.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: I've talked to Judge Lavinia. These mafiosi have been declared outlaws under the New Urban Management Act...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: No one is going to hold you responsible if you accidentally shoot them.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: So, take a deep breath, and hold your weapon firm. We're protecting Justice Lavinia, protecting the courthouse, and protecting ourselves.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: But, Eirene...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Listen.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: The cheering. It's getting nearer and nearer.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: The parade will reach Court Square in just a few more minutes.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: How will the people interpret what they see? They're the ones who will pass judgment.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: The law needs only facts, doesn't it?
Eirene's voice is trembling, but the crossbow in her hand is firm. Suddenly, Lyudmila feels like she is looking at a stranger.
The beast masked-figures on one side, the truck drivers on the other, like they are standing on two sides of a river.
There is no weapon on the ground, only shattered boxes. The weapons are in their hands.
Everyone hears the sounds filling the air.
The rumbling of floats, impromptu band performance, the spirited yelling of acrobats... the parade draws ever closer.
Then, sounds that are fainter, but even more audible. The sound of guns being loaded and locked, Arts units being activated, crossbow safeties pins being unlocked...
There is nowhere to hide. There is nowhere to run.
No one has moved, yet. At the first shot, the dammed river will burst, and the tide of madness will wash over everything.
No one speaks. Nerves are wound to the very tightest. Everyone is listening to the sounds, and their own racing heartbeats.
A new day will dawn upon Nuova Volsinii soon.
But the night is long.
